title: Longitudinal outcomes of bone-anchored maxillary protraction treatment
html: Bone-anchored maxillary protraction (BAMP) is a well-tolerated treatment for Class III orthopedic effects during adolescence. BAMP aims to improve Class III skeletal relationships with minimal dentoalveolar compensations, in the hope of reducing the need for orthognathic surgery. Our aim was to evaluate the short- and long-term effects of BAMP on measures of tooth and jaw positions and definitive treatment outcomes in patients with Class III malocclusion treated with (+) and without (−) BAMP during adolescence.
